learning_objective: ⚖️ Explore how deeply rooted social differences—gender, religion, and caste—shape, challenge, and sometimes distort democratic politics!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: पितृसत्ता (ऐसी व्यवस्था जिसमें पुरुषों को महिलाओं से अधिक अधिकार और शक्ति दी जाती है)
नारीवादी (वह व्यक्ति जो पुरुषों और महिलाओं के लिए समान अधिकारों में विश्वास करता है)
सांप्रदायिकता (राजनीति में धर्म का उपयोग यह मानकर करना कि एक धर्म दूसरे से श्रेष्ठ है)
धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य (वह राज्य जिसका अपना कोई आधिकारिक धर्म नहीं होता)
जातिवाद (यह मानना कि एक जाति के लोग एक अलग सामाजिक समुदाय बनाते हैं और अन्य जातियों से श्रेष्ठ हैं)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Society enforces a 'Sexual Division of Labour' where women handle unpaid domestic work and men do paid public work. Feminist movements fight for equality. In Indian politics, women's representation in the Lok Sabha is historically very low, though local bodies reserve 33% seats for them.

Religion becomes a problem when expressed in politics in exclusive and partisan terms (Communalism). It happens when people believe followers of one religion belong to a completely different community, often leading to polarization, riots, and violence.

To combat communalism, India adopted secularism. There is no official state religion (unlike Buddhism in Sri Lanka or Islam in Pakistan). The Constitution provides freedom to profess any religion and prohibits discrimination on religious grounds.

Parties choose candidates based on the caste composition of the constituency. They appeal to caste sentiments to secure 'vote banks'. However, no parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of a single caste, proving that voters look beyond just caste.

Politics also influences the caste system! Castes try to become bigger by incorporating neighboring sub-castes. New kinds of caste groups come into the political arena, like 'backward' and 'forward' caste coalitions, changing how society functions.

fun_activity.title: 🧹 The Invisible Chore List
fun_activity.instructions: Make a list of all daily household chores (cooking, cleaning, washing, getting groceries). Next to each, write who does it in your house. Add up the total hours. This simple list visually demonstrates the 'Sexual Division of Labour' that feminists challenge globally!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define 'Communalism'. It's not just about practicing a religion; it's the belief that religion is the principal basis of a social community.
📌 Be ready to explain the dual relationship: How Caste affects Politics AND how Politics affects Caste (they are two different answers!).
📌 Know the reasons why the caste system is breaking down in modern India (Urbanization, literacy, occupational mobility, and the Constitution).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Equal Remuneration Act of 1976 provides that equal wages should be paid for equal work regardless of gender.
⭐ Gandhiji believed that 'religion can never be separated from politics', but by religion, he meant moral values drawn from all religions, not communalism.
⭐ Untouchability, the worst extreme of the caste hierarchy, has been legally abolished by the Indian Constitution.
